widgets_values:
ROLE: Generate a brand-new photograph from scratch. This is NOT an edit of Image 1 — do not copy, reuse, or upscale any pixels from Image 1.

INPUTS (reference each by index):
- Image 1 = CONTENT reference ONLY (identity, outfit, location, lighting, style). Its framing / crop / shot type is IRRELEVANT and must be ignored entirely.
- Image 2 = CAMERA, COMPOSITION, CROP, and POSE reference (HIGHEST PRIORITY). The output frame must match Image 2.

[1] CAMERA & CROP — mirror Image 2 EXACTLY (top priority):
Reproduce Image 2's exact shot type, crop boundary, camera distance, focal length, and angle. The camera has physically moved to Image 2's position, so re-render the whole scene (subject + background) from this new viewpoint with correct new perspective, scale, and parallax.
- The output frame must show EXACTLY the same portion of the body that Image 2 shows — no more, no less. Whatever Image 2 includes, the output includes; whatever Image 2 crops out, the output crops out.
- If Image 2 shows the full body (feet included), the output is a full-body shot with feet included. If Image 2 shows only part of the body, the output is cropped at the exact same point.
- Match Image 2's subject scale (how much of the frame the person fills), headroom, and crop boundary precisely.
- IGNORE Image 1's framing entirely — do not inherit Image 1's crop, whether it is wider OR tighter than Image 2.
- Do NOT crop tighter than Image 2 and do NOT crop wider than Image 2. Do not add or remove any body part relative to Image 2.

[2] POSE & EXPRESSION — follow Image 2:
The model holds Image 2's pose. Treat this as a different frame from the same session (shot moments apart), so allow subtle, natural variation in: facial expression (natural, not a frozen duplicate), head tilt, gaze direction, and the angle of body parts not fixed by the pose — so the whole moment reads as one coherent, naturally captured frame.

[3] KEEP FROM Image 1 (CONTENT ONLY — never framing):
- Same model: face, identity, hair, skin tone, body proportions
- Same outfit: exact garment, color, fabric, fit, details
- Same location and same background elements/objects (same scene seen from the new angle — do not add, remove, or rearrange anything)
- Same lighting, color grading, and photographic style

OUTPUT: One real, photorealistic photograph where subject and background share Image 2's single camera position and crop. Natural skin texture, believable detail, not an AI edit of Image 1. No watermark, no text, no logos.
